resources.note: Text and JSON from the agent and incoming messages are labelled untrusted reference data. Local URIs use the confined content resolver.

model.effort.note: The host qualifies efforts against the model's protocol catalogue. Anthropic Messages maps supported efforts to native thinking settings and enables manual thinking when the output limit allows its minimum budget. Chat Completions and OpenAI Responses receive the effort value. An effort rejection triggers a retry with the effort configuration omitted for the rest of the work attempt.

skills.note: Selected local skills are listed by name and description. The skill tool activates their instructions and reads text or JSON companion files within their package.

mcpServers.note: The Host discovers tools using its qualified local stdio and remote Streamable HTTP transports.

directories.note: Additional admitted roots are indexed for file tools. Shell calls stage them under /directories/<index> on Linux and expose their staged paths in ARGENTIC_DIRECTORY_<index> on macOS. Overlapping shell roots are refused.

instance.new.note: Each new instance has a fresh conversation. Shared and named instances retain their conversation in memory until the Host run ends. A Host restart interrupts active runs.

read.note: Direct file tools enforce the compiled policy. The shell sandbox exposes a filtered workspace snapshot and the system files needed to run programs. Qualification refuses shell with an explicit outside denial or a deny or ask rule that overlaps a required runtime mount.

write.note: Direct file tools enforce the compiled policy. Shell changes to regular workspace files are published only with a blanket write grant.

shell.note: Shell rules match the command text, including each subcommand of a compound command, but not programs that a matched command starts. Dynamic command words and shell constructs that indirectly execute commands take the most restrictive explicit shell rule. Shell requires system Bubblewrap and working PID and user namespaces on Linux ARM64 or x86-64, or Seatbelt on macOS ARM64.

network.note: The OS blocks direct shell egress. HTTP and HTTPS clients use the local Argentic proxy, which applies every effective host rule and requires a person for ask. Clients that ignore the proxy environment have no network access. Private addresses require an explicit IP rule.

mcp.note: Each tool is evaluated by server/tool across the effective policy. Ask requires a person and is denied without one.

forceSubmissionOnCorrection.description: Force the result tool by name after a missing required submission. Defaults to true. If the provider rejects the named choice, Argentic retries with required (any for Anthropic Messages) and only the result tool. If the provider rejects that form, Argentic disables forced choice for the rest of the attempt and restores all tools. Argentic uses automatic tool selection on requests that deliver steering and on Anthropic Messages requests with manual extended thinking.

compaction.description: Summarize older conversation turns before reaching the configured provider context window.

enabled.description: Defaults to true when the provider context window is configured.

threshold.description: Fraction of the window, strictly between zero and one. Defaults to 0.8.

keepRecentTurns.description: Positive count of recent assistant turns to retain verbatim. Defaults to four.
